  • 剖析韓國K-pop偶像出道年齡日益幼態化的產業結構與商業獲利邏輯。
  • 了解「K-pop教父」李秀滿重新出發後，如何以低齡跨國女團再度掀起市場話題與熱議。
  • 深入探討星夢背後的高昂補習成本如何演變成階級競爭，以及年幼偶像所承受的身心健康代價。

摘要

李秀滿攜低齡女團強勢回歸市場

由被譽為「K-pop教父」的李秀滿所創立的A2O娛樂，推出全新女團A2O LIGHT，出道新曲迅速登上韓國音源榜冠軍。然而，引發外界高度關注的是該團平均年齡僅15歲，最小成員甚至只有13歲，國中生年紀的出道引發了大眾對當前偶像生態的廣泛討論。

出道年齡逐年下修背後的商業算盤

數據顯示韓國偶像的出道年齡正逐年下降，這背後的主要推動力來自經紀公司的獲利考量。由於培養練習生的沉沒成本極高，且近半數團體在出道未滿三年便宣告解散，使得公司傾向讓偶像提早出道，藉此拉長其在市場上的黃金吸金週期。

偶像補習班盛行與家庭財力的階級競爭

隨著全球化競爭加劇，經紀公司對語言與各項技能的要求日益嚴苛，導致選秀門檻提早降至十歲左右。這股趨勢催生了昂貴的偶像補習班文化，使練習生培育從單純的才華比拼，逐漸轉化為考驗家庭經濟實力與階級資源的昂貴賭博。

幼年成名的身心重擔與社會倫理隱憂

過早踏入演藝圈的低齡偶像，必須承受高壓訓練所帶來的生理與身心失調，同時還得面對缺乏隱私與網路惡意的衝擊。儘管官方訂有未成年保護法規，但日常練習難以落實監督，更引發了過度兒童性化以及過早剝奪青少年探索多元人生發展選擇權的道德爭議。

=============

最近韓國演藝圈出現一支超級年輕的女團，才剛出道，第一首歌就在29小時內衝上韓國最大音樂串流平台Melon的排行榜冠軍，成績相當驚人。更驚人的是，這支女團總共9個人，平均年齡只有15歲，最小的3位成員，竟然只有13歲！如果在台灣，大概就是國一、國二的年紀。但真正引起話題的，還有她們背後的製作人，竟然是有「K-pop教父」之稱的李秀滿。74歲的教父，帶著一群13歲少女重出江湖，這是什麼組合？而且，現在的K-pop偶像，真的有必要這麼年輕嗎？

item.itunes:title: 強調素人參政、撇清黨派，第三勢力拚翻轉！美期中選舉掀「政黨切割潮」，選民最後卻含淚看黨投票？【TODAY 看世界】
item.itunes:author: TODAY 看世界
item.itunes:summary:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tcnsa_zv04U

值得閱讀的理由

  • 解析候選人為何刻意淡化政黨色彩，改以職業經歷與個人特質爭取選民認同。
  • 說明政黨不受歡迎、經濟焦慮與對政治老手的不滿，如何改變美國選戰策略。
  • 揭示「反建制」形象與實際投票行為之間的落差，並比較政黨標籤在不同選舉層級的影響。

摘要

從政黨色彩轉向個人品牌

選舉期間，候選人往往以政黨代表色彰顯政治立場，但作者指出，近年有些人開始改用個人風格建立品牌。以台北市長參選人沈伯洋為例，他的主要競選視覺採用橘色，搭配「讓台北流動」的口號，而不是以民進黨的綠色為主。這並非完全切斷政黨連結，而是呈現候選人不必只靠政黨認同，也能凸顯自身形象的趨勢。

政治素人與反建制形象

美國選戰也出現相似現象，而且更加鮮明。消防員、咖啡師、歌手、牧師、記者與運動教練等不同背景的參選者，常先介紹自己的職業與人生經歷，而非大聲宣示黨籍。部分候選人甚至以獨立身分參選，或在廣告中批評自己所屬政黨。作者指出，自2016年以來，進入國會的政治圈外人士比例明顯上升，政治新手因此成為候選人與政黨塑造新鮮感的重要資源。

淡化黨籍背後的政治盤算

候選人看似與政黨保持距離，卻不一定真的脫離政黨。部分自稱素人的參選者，仍獲得大量政黨資金支持；政黨也可能安排候選人退選，替特定人選鋪路。作者說明，兩大黨都在操作「不想當典型政客」的形象，因為選民對政黨愈來愈反感。民調顯示，不喜歡兩大黨的民眾比例升高，自認為獨立選民的人數也創下新高；在「負面黨派認同」盛行的環境裡，選民往往不是出於喜愛而支持某黨，而是為了阻止另一黨勝選。候選人淡化黨籍，便有機會讓對手陣營的選民暫時放下成見。

經濟焦慮與對老政治的厭倦

作者歸納出另外兩項原因。首先是生活成本與經濟壓力：物價上漲時，選民更在意油價與日常開支，執政黨候選人也更容易因政府施政受到責難。部分共和黨參選人因此與川普及黨內建制派拉開距離；民主黨候選人則試圖回應選民對政黨過度強調身分政治、忽略民生議題的不滿。其次，選民厭倦長期執政的老面孔，期待政治出現變化。以新職業、新世代候選人展現「換一批人試試看」，便成為爭取支持的策略。

選民喜歡反建制，投票時仍看政黨

不過，選民口頭上喜歡政治圈外人士，不代表投票時就會選擇第三黨或跨黨支持。調查顯示，雖然許多美國人不滿兩大黨，真正願意投給第三黨的人仍然很少。政治學實驗也發現，選民喜歡「我和華府那群人不一樣」的說法，但候選人是否真是政治素人，影響並沒有想像中大；選民更在意的是反建制的形象。然而，政黨認同依然強大：自2012年以來，多數州的參議員選舉結果都與該州最近一次總統大選的勝方一致，2016年甚至有34州在總統與參議員選舉中選出同一政黨。

地方選舉更看重候選人本身

候選人的個人形象並非毫無作用。研究發現，選舉層級愈地方化，選民愈可能跨越黨派界線；在南卡羅來納州，川普支持者於國會選舉分裂投票的比例只有5%，到了郡議會選舉升至23%，警長選舉則接近一半。這顯示地方選舉中，選民更重視候選人的經驗、辦事能力與親民程度；但在國會或總統大選裡，政黨標籤仍較有影響力。作者最後將這股風潮解讀為選民對現況失望、期待嘗試新選擇的表現，並邀請觀眾思考：投票時政黨有多重要，自己是否曾跨黨派投票，以及這種選擇是否會因地方與總統選舉而不同。

For instance, Shen Po-yang, running for Taipei mayor this year for the DPP, avoided the party's signature green in his main campaign visuals, opting instead for a warm, sunny orange paired with the slogan "Make Taipei Flow." While he didn't explicitly say this was to. downplay his green camp ties—since green elements still appear in other materials—it shows that candidates don't have to rely solely on party identity; they can build their own political brand. This recent US midterm election saw a similar trend, and they took it even further. A group of baristas and firefighters looking to serve the public are racing for Congress, each emphasizing they aren't career politicians; some are even dropping party affiliations entirely, or going so far as to criticize their own party in campaign ads. Isn't running for office usually about.

relying on the party's aura to attract votes? Why are these people desperately trying to act like they don't know their own parties? Hello everyone, I’m Fan Chi, and welcome to Fan Chi’s World View. It’s noted that many federal congressional candidates this year no longer lead their rallies by shouting their party; instead, they introduce themselves as pastors, journalists, or football coaches, hoping voters remember their personal traits rather than the party behind them. Most of those doing this are. political novices; studies show that while over 70%of newly elected US representatives used to be political veterans, since 2016, the share of political outsiders entering Congress has risen significantly, now accounting for half. In the Democratic House races , we’ve seen firefighters, baristas, and even a Latin singer who performed for nearly 30 years and opened up their microphone for the campaign. The Republicans are also playing the novice card, sending a TV sports reporter to run for senator; their support is even.

rivaling the incumbent Democratic lieutenant governor, aiming to snatch the seat. These candidates from vastly different backgrounds are all trying to use their personal professional experience to dilute their party labels and distinguish themselves from polished, traditional politicians. Beyond downplaying party colors, some opt out of party labels entirely, such as a mechanic running as an independent to challenge a wealthy incumbent Republican senator, pitting grassroots labor against a moneyed politician, along with former Green Berets and. former tank commanders running as independents. For conservative voters, this tough, patriotic image is often more persuasive than any party label and much easier to win over voters. Independent voters; interestingly, even veteran politicians have started following suit. A veteran Democratic congressman of 20 years is now emphasizing his roots as a fifth-generation lumberjack, and a sitting representative claims they once skipped a congressional vote to return.

home and fish for salmon, all to stress they are locals, not high-and-mighty politicians. But are these candidates who "don't act like politicians" truly unaffiliated with political parties? Some candidates campaign as pastors, never mentioning party ties on stage, yet they are backed by millions in Democratic funding. Democrats may even force their own candidates to drop out at the last minute to clear the path for these specific political outsiders. The Republican Party has similar tactics, with campaign committees spending money on ads for their own candidates that highlight their. willingness to defy their own party. Voters support a party not because they love it, but because they fear the other. party winning even more. In polls released this month, more than 70%of voters in both parties shared this sentiment. imposing tariffs or challenging Iran, these international achievements are a burden for candidates who must face their constituents daily. different professions is meant to show they can bring a new atmosphere and that it's time for a shake-up. But are voters really buying it?   • 深入剖析法國高中生示威背後的體制危機，揭示高福利國家如何因教育資源匱乏與破爛校舍引爆全民怒火。

摘要

高中生怒火燎原：從破舊校舍演變成全法暴動

作者指出，這場席捲法國的大規模示威，導火線並非傳統的勞工抗爭，而是一群僅 14 至 17 歲的高中生。抗議起源於巴黎郊區的高中，學生們因面臨師資嚴重缺乏、校舍老舊破損甚至有動物出沒而發起罷課堵校，短短時間便蔓延至全法國上百所學校。在巴黎北郊聖但尼等外來移民與貧困人口集中的地區，開學時有高達六成的國高中師資不足，凸顯了嚴重的教育資源分配不均。然而，法國警方採取強勢鎮壓手段，動用鎮暴裝備造成多名學生重傷與數千人被捕，強硬執法進一步點燃公憤，吸引黃背心運動支持者與廣大民眾加入，使訴求擴大為抗議高物價、薪資停滯與公共服務低落的全國性反政府浪潮。

預算遭退休金吞噬：高福利招牌下的財政黑洞

面對教育崩潰的慘況，作者深入探討法國身為高稅負國家的財政困境。事實上，法國教育部與內政部有高達三成預算被公務員退休金吃光，加上過去退休年齡偏低，政府長年入不敷出。當前法國的公共債務已飆升至 GDP 的 119%，鉅額的利息支出迫使政府陷入借債償債的惡性循環。儘管總統馬克宏試圖將退休年齡延後以挽救財政，卻引爆全民反彈，陷入勞工不願縮減福利、青年又爭取不到教育資源的世代僵局；馬克宏也因政策偏向菁英被貼上「富人總統」標籤，滿意度跌入谷底，面臨嚴峻的執政信任危機。

高福利時代終結與對台灣的深刻警思

作者進一步點出，人口紅利消失與高齡化正全面衝擊歐洲各國，過去「免費教育、便宜健保與優渥假期」的生活模式已難以維持。在民主選票的政治現實下，沒有投票權的孩童教育資源往往最先遭到犧牲。對照台灣現況，作者提出深切憂慮，批評政客競相推動「65 歲以上免繳健保費」等缺乏財政紀律的討好選民政策，呼籲大眾反思：在國家資源有限的情況下，究竟應優先改善年輕世代的教育與買房負擔，還是持續擴大長輩的醫療福利，避免讓下一代承擔無以為繼的財政苦果。

法國又双叒叕抗議了，但這次，不一樣。點燃這波大規模示威潮的，竟然是一群年紀只有14到17歲的高中生。在台灣，家長們會說，高中生不好好用功搞這些有的沒的？問題就出在他們很想讀書，但竟然沒老師教，教室還很破甚至有小動物開趴踢，然後這場學運就從巴黎郊區的高中，一路蔓延到法國各大主要城市，上個週末還升高成暴動、趁火打劫事件。今天我們就要來仔細看看，這場已經燒了一個月的怒火，是怎麼一回事？

As mentioned, Taiwanese couriers often think foreigners won't face serious consequences if caught, assuming it's.

In principle, they will be barred from entering Japan. "I didn't know what was inside" is not a valid excuse to escape. legal responsibility. The second group is the victims. Japanese police state that money stolen in these scams is rarely recovered. The syndicate profits from a single success, while the victims bear the loss alone. A new system is expected to launch in 2028; even travelers from visa-exempt countries will be required to provide details like accommodation and travel plans for advance screening. The actions of a few may add hurdles for all Taiwanese visiting Japan and damage the image of Taiwanese people there. For many Taiwanese, Japan is a familiar country they can visit at a moment's notice.

But when you see online ads offering free trips to Japan, simple work, and high pay, you really need to think twice. I really don't have much sympathy for these criminals. Whether they're acting as money mules or smuggling drugs, haven't the warnings over these past few years been enough? Who would actually believe someone who still claims they didn't know they were participating in a scam or didn't know they were carrying illegal drugs? Getting locked up is just what they deserve. On top of that, Japanese society is already pushing back strongly against overtourism, so adding these transnational crimes is just pouring salt in the wound. We always. feel that going to Japan is as familiar as visiting a neighbor, but a few bad apples will eventually spoil the whole bunch. With more and more news of Taiwanese committing crimes in Japan, do you think this will worsen the Japanese perception of Taiwanese tourists in the future? 台灣人赴日犯罪激增：從觀光熱潮到跨國詐騙

作者指出，台灣人熱愛前往日本旅遊，但近年卻出現越來越多以觀光名義赴日從事詐騙的案例。光是近兩個月就至少發生四起台灣人涉案事件，金額從數百萬到數千萬日圓不等。根據外交部統計，台灣人在日本涉及詐騙的人數從2023年的4人暴增至2025年的50人。許多嫌犯受到網路上「海外打工兼旅遊、邊玩邊賺錢」的廣告吸引，甚至誤信「外國人被抓不會有事」的謊言，淪為犯罪組織的棋子。

犯罪集團的盤算：為何台灣人成為「闇黑打工」首選目標？

作者分析，幕後主謀涵蓋日本黑道、中國犯罪團夥以及自台灣轉移陣地的詐騙集團。日本因高齡少子化與政府強力宣導，本土犯罪人力短缺，轉而招募外國人。犯罪集團特別相中台灣人，主因在於年輕人對日本戒心極低，且享有免簽證待遇，犯案後能迅速離境使警方難以追查。對集團而言，這些不會日語、僅靠翻譯軟體出面取款的車手純屬「拋棄式工具人」，即便被逮也不會危及核心組織。
